newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.1 pct in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.1 pct in speculative trade.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.10 percent in the commercial foreign exchange market in speculative trading as some banks squared off positions ahead of Friday's mayoral run-off elections, dealers said.
"Banks are getting rid of short positions ahead of November 15, when markets will be closed due to the second round of the municipal elections," a dealer said.
In the morning session, the real fell a maximum of 0.24 percent to 1.0320 per greenback. But, due to a scarcity of reais, the currency pared losses to end down 0.10 percent at 1.0305 per dollar.
In the floating exchange rate market, the real also dropped 0.03 percent to end at 1.0353 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real ended flat at 1.075 per greenback.
